A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga–Satake Correspondences

definitions.ks10:context:surface: Varieties are complex; cohomology is rational Betti cohomology. (S,h) is a primitively amply polarized K3 surface, h²=2d. V=h-perpendicular in H²(S,Q) has dimension 21 and signature (2,19) for the cup form q. T=NS(S)_Q-perpendicular is contained in V, contains the period plane, and has dimension at least two. Q(1) shifts Hodge types by (-1,-1); the Hodge circle acts on type (p,q) by exp(i(p-q)θ).
definitions.ks10:context:exact-target: Fix a rational quadratic polarization Q on T, the full even Clifford construction, an invertible odd right multiplier identifying parity spaces, a rational weight-one polarization, and a specified isogenous abelian realization A_S with W_S=H¹(A_S,Q). These data determine κ_S:T→W_S⊗W_S→H²(A_S×A_S,Q) in the ordered mixed Künneth summand. Exact realization means Γ_S∈CH²(S×A_S×A_S)_Q with (p_AA)_*(cl(Γ_S)∪p_S*x)=κ_S(x) for every x∈T, with every normalization retained.
definitions.ks10:context:clifford: H is rational of weight two and K3 type, with h²⁰=h⁰²=1 and only types (2,0),(1,1),(0,2). Q is nondegenerate, of sign ε=±1 on the oriented period plane and the opposite sign on its orthogonal complement. The relation is v²=Q(v,v). For H²⁰=C(e₁+i e₂), Q(e_j,e_j)=ε and e₁⊥e₂, J=εe₁e₂ and g_θ=cos θ+J sin θ act by left multiplication on the full parity spaces P_H^±=C^±(H,Q), with the i-eigenspace of L_J designated (1,0).
definitions.ks10:context:algebraic-realization: A chosen weight-one polarization gives j_P:P∨(-1)≅P. For f:H(1)→Hom(P,M), its tensor form is H→M⊗P∨(-1)→M⊗P. When H⊂H²(S,Q), algebraic realization means exactly this restricted action of a codimension-two rational cycle on S×A_M×A_P, with algebraic target projectors available to remove other Künneth components.
definitions.ks10:context:generic-representations: The recovery section assumes Hg(V)=SO(V,q) for the rank-21 primitive K3 space, not a genericity condition on the witness abelian variety. In the joint group of V, U=H¹(B,Q), and W^±=C^±(V,q), the distinguished rational Lie ideal is g≅so(V,q). Its complex spin module Δ has dimension 2¹⁰.
definitions.ks10:context:very-general: On a connected complex manifold, 'very general' means outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets. Specialization concerns actual rational cycle classes, not merely flat classes that are Hodge, and retains the entire prescribed class and its coefficients.
definitions.ks10:context:correspondence-degree: For smooth projective P,Q, Z∈CH^a(P×Q)_Q acts H^j(P)→H^{j+2e}(Q)(e), e=a-dim P, by pullback, cup with cl(Z), and pushforward. Composition subtracts the dimension of the intermediate variety from the sum of codimensions.

definitions.ks30:context:hc-ghc: Coefficients are rational. HC is surjectivity CH^r(X)_Q→H^{2r}(X,Q)∩H^{r,r}(X) for smooth projective complex X. N^pH^j(X,Q) is the sum, over closed B⊂X of codimension at least p, of kernels of restriction to X\B; GHC identifies this with the largest rational sub-Hodge structure with both Hodge indices at least p. Later N^p=H^j for p≤0. For a projective K3 S, T_S=NS(S)_Q-perpendicular in H²(S,Q) with its actual cup form q has signature (2,20−ρ(S)).
definitions.ks30:context:exact-tensor: For a K3-type quadratic space (T,q), use v²=q(v,v), the full W=C⁺(T,q), and the left complex structure L_J for J=e₁e₂ when T²⁰=C(e₁+i e₂) with an oriented positive orthonormal pair. Fix H¹(A,Q)=W, a rational nonisotropic w∈T, and rational polarization E. The exact map is j_w:T(1)→End(W), j_w(v)(a)=vaw. In End(W)=W⊗W∨, apply (E^flat)^−1 to the dual slot after untwisting to obtain ι_{w,E}:T→W⊗W⊂H²(A²,Q). The choice of w need not be a Hodge vector. 'Standard' means this specified map, not an arbitrary embedding.
definitions.ks30:context:quadratic-locus: The hyperbolic plane U has Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,0]]. P=U⊕D₈(−1)⊕D₄(−1); T_P=U⊕U(2)⊕D₄(−1); V_P=(T_P)_Q≅U_Q²⊥⟨−1⟩⁴ has dimension eight and signature (2,6). An ample P-polarization is a primitive embedding P→NS(S) whose image contains an ample class. U_P=P_Q-perpendicular retains rank eight at Picard jumps, when it may strictly contain T_S.
definitions.ks30:context:cycles-and-projectors: Cohomology is rational Betti unless an integral lattice is specified; integral cohomology is modulo torsion. A cycle Z∈CH^r(M×N)_Q acts H^k(M)→H^{k+2r−2dim M}(N) by pullback, product and pushforward, with the corresponding Tate twist. Projectors mean algebraic correspondences acting idempotently on cohomology, not necessarily idempotence in Chow.
definitions.ks30:context:exterior-powers: For S, set N=NS(S)_Q, T=N-perpendicular, V=T(1). A point o, a divisor basis D_i and its inverse intersection matrix b^{ij} give π₀=[o]×S, π₄=S×[o], π_N=Σb^{ij}D_i×D_j and π_T=Δ−π₀−π₄−π_N. Products of π_T and Alt_k=(1/k!)Σsgn(σ)σ cut out Λ^kT⊂H^{2k}(S^k,Q), self-adjointly with nondegenerate exterior pairing. Algebraic coefficient extension means scalar extension of the rational cycle-class image, with rational descent H_Q∩(A_Q⊗K)=A_Q.
definitions.ks30:context:abelian-covers: B is an indecomposable principally polarized abelian surface, M=O_B(H) a symmetric principal theta bundle, and χ∈Pic⁰(B)[4] has exact order four. A normalized section d∈H⁰(B,M²) cuts out a smooth D avoiding B[2]. Work on algebraic affine section charts ℓ(d)=1 of the six-dimensional parameter space. π:B'→B is the degree-two isogeny for χ², with π_*O=O⊕χ²; choose a trivialization of π*χ². Let L=π*(Mχ) and X→B' be z²=π*d. δ is the sheet involution and j the commuting lift of inversion from the normalized symmetric linearization of L. U_X=H²(X,Q)^{j=1,δ=−1}.
definitions.ks30:context:gauss-selections: On the good open of geom:gauss-generic, the regular Gauss fibers on D are {±x₁,…,±x₄}. Over their regular-value open R⊂P¹, the 16 selections contain one point from each opposite pair. s[p] flips the chosen signed point p. The two parity covers and their smooth projective completions C_± need not be connected; they share a coherent half-sum assignment.
definitions.ks30:context:pencil-and-lattices: V here denotes the integral anti-invariant lattice of Y of signature (2,14), not T(1) from the earlier criterion section; U is its rational rank-eight summand with the Y-pairing. The lattice enlargement called M in the pencil section is unrelated to the theta bundle M. A section pencil is d_t=d₀+t d₁ on the original affine t-line, ℓ(d₀)=1, ℓ(d₁)=0, with leading section smooth and avoiding two-torsion.
definitions.ks30:context:period-stack: A polarized ADE K3 is a normal surface with rational double points whose minimal resolution is a K3, with a primitive ample relative Picard class. A smooth quasi-polarization is primitive big and nef. Fix a positive primitive h in Λ_K3; D_h is a component of the isotropic positive-line domain in h-perpendicular; Γ_h fixes h and preserves that component. P_h=[Γ_h\D_h] is the integral period stack. Contractions are canonical polarized contractions; scalar automorphisms of representing line bundles are removed by the relative-Picard convention.
definitions.ks30:context:two-squares: For one fixed original pencil O⊂A¹_t, compare a smooth projective K3 family S→O and a smooth projective connected-surface family X→O. The first substitution t=s+u² gives threefolds, fixed compactifications and a degree-three correspondence before b is chosen. The second s=b+v² gives the conic u²+v²=(t−b)w²; its two complete components at t=b give difference cylinders. φ between the degree-two subvariations need not be an isometry; in the geometric application φ* q_X=2q_Y.
definitions.ks30:context:full-half-spin: For U of dimension eight and signature (2,6), W=C⁺(U,q) has rational dimension 128. Over C its left action consists of eight copies of each eight-dimensional half-spin S_±. Recovery uses both ordered tensor orientations and ordinary tensor flip; on the mixed H¹⊗H¹ summand the geometric interchange acts as minus that ordinary flip.

definitions.milne:context:fields-and-reduction: Fix Qbar⊂C, a prime p and a p-adic place w of Qbar. F=algebraic closure of F_p, K₀=Frac W(F), and C_w is the completion of Qbar at w. K₀ and an algebraic closure of it are regarded as subfields of C_w. Good reduction means after descent to a number field and finite extension at the chosen place. The prime and place stay fixed; no comparison between different places is asserted.
definitions.milne:context:realizations: For X/F, H_v^{2r}(X)(r) denotes ℓ-adic cohomology over k_ℓ=Q_ℓ for ℓ≠p, and crystalline cohomology extended from K₀ to k_p=C_w for v=p. Traces use the top Tate twist and send zero-cycle classes to degrees. Hodge-class specializations are absolute-Hodge/smooth-proper away from p and de Rham–crystalline at p. Tensor operations, divisor classes and homomorphisms use the same comparison normalizations. First crystalline cohomology remains over K₀ when filtrations are constructed.
definitions.milne:context:rational-homomorphisms: Work up to isogeny: Hom⁰(X,Y)=Hom(X,Y)⊗Q. For a rational homomorphism f, pullback on H¹ extends to the exterior algebra; if Nf is integral, f*=N^(−2r)(Nf)* on H^{2r}, simultaneously in every realization. Rational divisor coefficients and denominators divisible by p are allowed after inverting p.
definitions.milne:context:lefschetz-space: Lef^r(X) is rational divisor-polynomial expressions of codimension r modulo numerical equivalence. A simultaneous rational Lefschetz class is the tuple of realizations of one fixed element of this Q-space, not merely a tuple lying separately in its local scalar spans. The manuscript imports injective realization, perfect complementary pairing, stability under homomorphism pushforward, and hard Lefschetz plus its inverse on these subspaces.
definitions.milne:def:lefschetz-pairing: A tuple α=(α_v)_v with α_v∈H_v^{2r}(X)(r) has the Lefschetz pairing property if for every δ∈Lef^{dim X−r}(X), all Tr_v(α_vδ_v) are images of one rational number. The rational number may depend on δ and α.
definitions.milne:context:finite-local-descent: Finite local-field descent means the isocrystal and indicated tensors descend to H₀, the maximal unramified subfield of a finite H/Q_p, with filtration over H; extension is to K₀H. A tensor-preserving identification respects a finite rational tensor family whose stabilizer is the chosen group, together with all comparison realizations.
definitions.milne:context:strong-admissibility: A full Bruhat–Tits stabilizer is the smooth group scheme fixing a point of the extended building; its identity component is parahoric. The cited strongly admissible triple (H,X_H,H_model) is Hodge type, has full stabilizer with connected special fiber, R-smooth centralizer of a maximal K₀-split torus, and reduced relative root system over K₀ when p=2. The source invokes R-smoothness only for products/extensions of induced split tori.
definitions.milne:context:tensor-isogeny-class: For x in the integral Hodge-type model, C_x is its abelian variety, D_x=H¹_cris(C_x/W(F))[1/p], and s_{α,0,x}, s_{α,ℓ,x} are canonical specialized tensors. I_x consists of y admitting one actual abelian quasi-isogeny C_x→C_y preserving the crystalline tensors and every prime-to-p tensor. Separate unrelated local linear maps do not define membership.
definitions.milne:context:weak-admissibility: For an isocrystal D/K₀ and finite K/K₀, a subspace L⊂D_K defines Fil^i=D_K for i≤0, Fil¹=L, Fil^i=0 for i≥2. For every subisocrystal P⊂D over the fixed K₀, t_H(P)=dim_K(P_K∩L), t_N(P) is its slope sum, v(p)=1. Weak admissibility requires t_H(D)=t_N(D) and t_H(P)≤t_N(P) for every such P. Finite local-field descent is separate, not inferred merely from weak admissibility over K₀.
definitions.milne:context:balanced-weil: A/Qbar has good reduction at w, a rational action of a CM field E with conjugation e↦bar e, and polarization λ whose Rosati restricts to conjugation. For V=H₁(A(C),Q), dim_E V=2s, s≥1, dim A=g=s[E:Q], and every E-embedding has Hodge multiplicities (s,s). The alternating polarization ψ satisfies ψ(ex,y)=ψ(x,bar e y). Balanced signatures are not the stronger split-Weil-type condition that a related Hermitian form have a half-dimensional isotropic subspace.
definitions.milne:def:weil-space: W_E^s(A)⊂Λ_Q^{2s}V∨⊗Q(s)=H^{2s}(A(C),Q(s)) is the rational subspace whose extension to a splitting field Ω of E is the direct sum over τ:E→Ω of Λ_Ω^{2s}V_τ∨⊗Q(s)_Ω, each determinant form extended by zero on the other eigenspaces. The sum is Galois stable. Balanced signatures make these rational classes Hodge classes.
definitions.milne:context:rosati-anti-linear-space: For the reduced polarization, U={u∈End⁰(A₀):u†=u and ue=bar e u for every e∈E}. The dichotomy tests invertibility in the rational endomorphism algebra. An invertible such u gives a divisor form D^u(x,y)=ψ₀(x,uy), nondegenerate separately on each same-embedding E-eigenspace.
definitions.milne:context:weil-similitude-group: On homology V, let c be the GSp multiplier and define G={a∈GSp(V,ψ)∩GL_E(V):det_E(a)=c(a)^s}, the equality taken in E⊗R with scalar right-hand side for every Q-algebra R. Its dual cohomological form uses inverse multiplier under contragredient group action; the pullback action of an individual endomorphism is separately distinguished in the filtration proof.
definitions.milne:context:fixed-good-theory: S₀ is the class of F-varieties whose connected components are products of abelian varieties and projective spaces. After applying Milne2009 Theorem 4.5 to CM rationality, fix one good theory R of rational Tate classes before varying A or γ. Its rational spaces are stable under pullback, inject into realizations, and contain CM Hodge specializations. Its native crystalline components are over K₀; equality to γ_{0,p} is after extension to C_w. This membership statement by itself asserts no algebraic cycle.
definitions.milne:context:two-transports-figure: The figure distinguishes CM transport A^n→C only on reductions a_CM:A₀^n→C₀, with γ₀=(a_CM j)*κ₀, from prescribed-filtration transport of a separately chosen balanced Weil variety Z, a_fl:Z₀^m→B₀, with a_fl*Fil¹H¹_dR(B)=(F_Z¹)^⊕m. Vertical arrows are good reduction. The caption explicitly claims no map between generic fibers; B may be local and need not be CM, and the auxiliaries need not coincide.

definitions.mixed_pure: A mixed column has both Hodge-circle weights +1,-1. A pure column has one; scalar conjugation may change this property.
definitions.polarization: A compatible rational Riemann form e satisfies e(ax,y)=e(x,bar(a)y); for u^2=-d, h_E(x,y)=e(x,uy)+u e(x,y), conjugate-linear first.
definitions.CM_supply: Images of full rational cohomology of CM abelian varieties under rational algebraic correspondences, with the appropriate Tate shifts; not just images of their Hodge classes.

contexts.statement: Actual Hodge-group independence for dimension-at-most-six complex abelian varieties with a unital imaginary-quadratic action.

definitions.group: J is the smallest rational algebraic group containing the actual Hodge circle of H^1(A,Q), and R=J^der.
definitions.commutant: Use the full actual End_Hdg(H^1(B,Q)), not just the supplied imaginary-quadratic subfield.
definitions.columns: Primitive matrix columns of the split full commutant; identify matrix copies admissibly and pair opposite CM embeddings.
definitions.scope: Only derived images and determinant-criterion condition (c); no conclusion about central characters, determinant supply (d), cycle algebraicity, or publication novelty.

contexts.statement: All-degree full-cohomology CM supply for the two Weil-manuscript families, retaining the reviewed actual-group theorem.

definitions.families: A is a complex abelian variety with a unital imaginary-quadratic E action, either dim A at most five, or dim A six with an actual compatible polarization whose rational homological E-Hermitian form is hyperbolic of signature (3,3).
definitions.supply: C^d(X) is the rational sum of images of algebraic correspondence maps H^{d-2j}(B,Q)(-j) to H^d(X,Q), for CM abelian varieties B including a point and all valid integer shifts j.
definitions.coefficients: k is the algebraic closure of Q inside C; scalar conjugation acts on coefficients of the fixed complex variety, not on the variety.
definitions.balance: One geometrically fixed finite list of CM embedding lines is chosen before testing any determinant monomial. Arbitrary repetitions and all scalar conjugations are required.
definitions.scope: The conclusion is CM supply and rational Hodge lifts, not unconditional algebraicity. Algebraicity additionally requires the separate CM Hodge theorem, not audited here.

contexts.statement: Applicability of the published CM Hodge theorem at openai/math commit 4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae to the reviewed DS-UNIVERSAL reduction.

definitions.CM_source: An ordinary complex CM abelian variety, including a point, with toric degree-one Hodge group as in DS-CONTEXT.
definitions.required_conclusion: Every rational class of type (r,r) in ordinary Betti H^{2r}(B,Q) is in the image of the rational algebraic cycle-class map CH^r(B)_Q.
definitions.scope: AG-UNIVERSAL and DS-UNIVERSAL remain accepted and unchanged; kernel replay and geometric statement fidelity are separate obligations.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute the surviving unformalized OpenAI manuscripts in Family 032 and Family 001 ('A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga-Satake Correspondences', 'Algebraic Kuga-Satake correspondences and Hodge conjectures on a K3 quadratic locus', 'Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers', and 'Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties'), which sit directly adjacent to the three K3/Weil-class Hodge manuscripts withdrawn on October 7, 2026 due to a stabilization-trace sign error: either (a) identify and certify a remaining mathematical gap, hidden hypothesis, sign/polarization mismatch, or unproved dependency in these manuscripts with an exact symbolic certificate, or (b) independently verify and certify a rigorous theorem/audit on their exact algebraic Hodge/Kuga-Satake reduction chain.

Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q). The following are equivalent: (i) some complex abelian B and α∈CH²(S×B)_Q induce a nonzero map α_*:V→H²(B,Q); (ii) some smooth connected projective surface Y admits a dominant generically finite morphism f:Y→S for which the trace f_* of the image of Λ²H⁰(Y,Ω¹_Y)→H⁰(Y,Ω²_Y) is nonzero; (iii) for any stipulated standard data on T, a cycle Γ_S exactly realizes κ_S as in eq:cycle-target. In this situation T=V. The same input realizes the standard full primitive Clifford construction with the cup form.

Fix a component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2d. If condition (i) or (ii) of main:generic holds very generally in that component, then every (S,h) in it has the exact prescribed cycle Γ_S for every stipulated standard datum on T(S). It suffices that, about each desired point, the input holds outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart; an algebraically very-general input suffices. Witness cycles, abelian varieties, and covers need not vary in a family.
If the hypothesis of main:specialization holds in the required polarized components in every degree, then every projective K3 surface has a cycle realizing its prescribed κ_S.

For complex abelian varieties P,Q, pullback identifies Hom(Q,P)⊗Q with Hom_HS(H¹(P,Q),H¹(Q,Q)). Arbitrary rational weight-one Hodge maps therefore act algebraically and independently on the two slots of an ordered tensor product of first cohomologies; they need not preserve chosen polarizations.

Every cohomological Künneth projector on a product of abelian varieties is induced by a rational algebraic correspondence. For U=H¹(B,Q), the mixed part of pullback along addition B×B→B injects H²(B,Q)=Λ²U into U⊗U by u∧v↦u⊗v−v⊗u.

Let E be a finite-dimensional rational vector space of cohomological maps and E_alg its subspace of actions of rational algebraic correspondences of a fixed degree. For every field extension K/Q, E∩(E_alg⊗K)=E_alg inside E⊗K. The assertion remains true after restricting actions to a specified rational source subspace.

Under the full-Hodge-group setting of main:generic, its nonzero correspondence condition (i) and surface-cover wedge-trace condition (ii) are equivalent. The implication from (ii) to a nonzero correspondence on V does not require the full Hodge-group hypothesis; the converse uses injectivity on V.

For H,Q and the sign/orientation conventions of context:clifford, P_H^± are polarizable weight-one Hodge structures; m^Q:H(1)→Hom(P_H^+,P_H^-), x↦L_x, is a rational Hodge embedding. Right multiplication by any fixed invertible odd Clifford element gives a rational Hodge isomorphism of the parity spaces. On a sufficiently small period chart their filtrations vary holomorphically and admit fixed rational polarizations.

If f:H(1)→Hom(P,M) is algebraically realized and a:M→M', b:P'→P are rational weight-one Hodge maps, then x↦a f(x)b is algebraically realized. This remains true under changing chosen duality isomorphisms, interchanging tensor factors with the appropriate Künneth sign, and rational Hodge identifications with isogenous abelian models.

In every sufficiently small full-dimensional marked polarized period chart, Hg(V)=SO(V,q) holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets. At every such point V is irreducible as a rational Hodge structure and T(S)=V.

Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q), let B be any complex abelian variety, U=H¹(B,Q), W^±=C^±(V,q), and let h be the Lie algebra of their joint Hodge group with V. Then h=g⊕k as commuting rational ideals, g≅so(V,q), and k is the kernel on V. The ideal k acts trivially on both W^±, and g acts there by the usual left spin action.

In the joint-group setting, U_C=(Δ⊗M)⊕M₀ and W_C^±=Δ⊗N_± as g_C-modules, where M₀ is trivial and dim N_±=2¹⁰. Every rational g-equivariant map U→W^± is a weight-one Hodge map, and Hom_HS(U,W^±)⊗C=Hom_g_C(U_C,W_C^±)≅Hom_C(M,N_±).
For the vector module V_C of so₂₁(C) and its spin module Δ, Hom_g_C(V_C,Δ⊗Δ) has dimension one. Neither Δ nor the trivial representation contains a copy of V_C.

Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q), and suppose some α∈CH²(S×B)_Q induces a nonzero V→H²(B,Q). For every ε₁,ε₂∈{+,-}, every abelian realization H¹(A_j,Q)=W^{ε_j}, and every rational Hodge map β:V→W^{ε₁}⊗W^{ε₂}⊂H²(A₁×A₂,Q), there exists Γ∈CH²(S×A₁×A₂)_Q whose action restricted to V is β. In particular the full primitive Clifford multiplication tensor and its prescribed even-Clifford realization are recovered.

Let p:X→D be a smooth proper holomorphic family of nonempty pure n-dimensional varieties over a connected complex manifold, equipped with a relative embedding X⊂D×P^N. Then there are a reduced complex quasi-projective scheme H, a smooth projective algebraic family U→H, and a holomorphic η:D→H^an such that X is its embedded analytic pullback.

Let f:M→R be a smooth projective algebraic family of relative dimension n over a smooth irreducible complex variety R of dimension b. If Z⊂M is flat over R with fibers of dimension n−2, then r↦cl([Z_r]_{n−2}) in H⁴(M_r,Q) is a section of R⁴f_*^an Q. For a flat rational θ∈H⁰(D,R⁴p_*Q), if θ_t is the class of a rational codimension-two algebraic cycle for very general t, then it is such a class for every t∈D.

For any primitively amply polarized (S₀,h), after shrinking a full-dimensional polarized period polydisc D about its period, there exist smooth proper holomorphic K3 and abelian families S→D and A→D. Fix a polarized moduli component. If the nonzero algebraic input of main:generic holds very generally, then at every (S₀,h) in that component the standard full primitive Clifford tensor is induced by a rational codimension-two cycle. The same holds for an input outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized chart about each desired point.

At any polarized K3 fiber, with q₀=q|_T, algebraic realization of primitive Clifford multiplication m^q on V implies algebraic realization of m^{q₀} on T. No full-Hodge-group hypothesis is imposed at this fiber.

Let q₀,q₁ be rational quadratic Hodge polarizations of the same K3-type Hodge structure T, allowing either overall sign under the stated period-plane convention. If T⊂H²(S,Q) and m^{q₀} is algebraically realized, then m^{q₁} is algebraically realized. No assumption that the polarization-change Hodge endomorphism is scalar or algebraic on S is made.

The unrestricted algebraicity assertion for the Kuga–Satake Hodge embedding is a particular rational Hodge-conjecture problem. The manuscript does not prove existence of its initial algebraic map and explicitly does not claim to resolve the unrestricted Kuga–Satake conjecture.
There exist an abelian variety B and an actual rational algebraic α∈CH²(S×B)_Q with α_*|_V nonzero. Motivated or absolute Hodge classes alone do not satisfy this existence input.

There exist a smooth connected projective surface Y and a dominant generically finite morphism f:Y→S with nonzero trace on the wedge image Λ²H⁰(Y,Ω¹_Y)→H⁰(Y,Ω²_Y). This is an existence input, equivalent to the correspondence input under Hg(V)=SO(V,q).

In the chosen degree-2d polarized component, either the actual nonzero-correspondence input or the wedge-trace surface-cover input holds very generally; locally the required quantifier is outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets in a full chart about each desired target.

For smooth projective complex varieties, Hodge decomposition, Poincaré duality, Lefschetz (1,1), hard Lefschetz and Hodge–Riemann relations hold; pullbacks, Gysin maps and products have their usual Hodge types.
Polarizable rational Hodge structures have Hodge complements and reductive rational Hodge groups, also for finite joint collections.

In characteristic zero, algebraic group homomorphisms have closed image and surjective differential onto its Lie algebra; unipotent groups have nonzero invariants in nonzero representations; a reductive Lie algebra is the sum of its center and simple ideals.

A complex K3 surface has rank-22 cup lattice and the stated Hodge numbers, a smooth 20-dimensional universal deformation and a local period isomorphism; fixing a nonzero integral (1,1) class cuts out the corresponding period hypersurface and extends its line bundle.

The full even Clifford construction of a polarized K3-type Hodge structure is polarizable of weight one; Clifford multiplication with an invertible right multiplier gives its standard Hodge embedding. No algebraicity theorem for that embedding is an input.

Finite-dimensional representations of complex semisimple Lie algebras are completely reducible and classified by highest weights; type B_n has the dominant/spin weights used in the text. Clifford basis and spin double-cover statements hold in characteristic zero.
H¹ contravariantly identifies complex abelian varieties up to isogeny with polarizable rational weight-one Hodge structures; a polarized complex torus is projective.
For smooth projective complex Y its Albanese is an abelian variety, and an Albanese map induces an isomorphism on holomorphic one-forms.
On smooth projective varieties, correspondences compose by pullback, intersection and proper pushforward with the indicated codimension, and cycle classes commute with these operations.

For a projective family over a noetherian base, every fixed-polynomial relative Hilbert scheme is projective with a flat universal subscheme; a uniform sufficiently high degree supplies its Grassmannian realization.

Flat finitely presented morphisms with smooth fibers are smooth. For proper flat families, the smooth-fiber locus is open. Sufficiently high powers of ample bundles on projective varieties are very ample and have vanishing higher cohomology; Riemann–Roch computes Euler characteristics from Chern classes.
If a Cartier equation is a nonzerodivisor on a closed subscheme Z of dimension at most k+1, Cartier pullback carries [Z]_{k+1} to the k-dimensional cycle of the cut with scheme multiplicities.

Proper holomorphic maps have coherent higher direct images. For coherent sheaves flat over a reduced base, fiber cohomology is upper semicontinuous; constant dimensions give local freeness and base change. Coherent sheaves on Stein spaces have vanishing higher cohomology.

Proper smooth submersions are locally differentiably trivial. Proper holomorphic images of closed analytic sets are analytic. Irreducible components of complex analytic sets are closed and locally finite, and are countable in a second-countable space.

Complex quasi-projective varieties admit projective resolutions. Closed analytic subvarieties of projective space and holomorphic maps of projective varieties are algebraic; projective coherent and analytic cohomology agree.

Let S be any projective K3 surface. Suppose that for one rational nonisotropic w∈T_S, one rational weight-one polarization and one full even-Clifford realization H¹(A,Q)=C⁺(T_S,q), the tensor of j_w(v)(a)=vaw is induced by a cycle in CH²(S×A²)_Q. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of every self-power S^m.

Let S be a smooth projective complex K3 surface with a rational isometric embedding of its actual transcendental cup-product space (T_S,q) into V_P. For every full realization H¹(A,Q)=C⁺(T_S,q), every rational nonisotropic w∈T_S and every rational polarization E of that weight-one structure, a cycle Γ_S∈CH²(S×A×A)_Q acts on every x∈T_S as exactly ι_{w,E}(x) in full H²(A²,Q). The same holds for any specified transported isogenous model. Moreover rational HC and GHC hold in every degree of S^m for every m≥1. All ample P-polarized surfaces, including Picard jumps, satisfy the embedding hypothesis.

P admits a primitive embedding in Λ_K3=U³⊕E₈(−1)² whose integral orthogonal complement is T_P=U⊕U(2)⊕D₄(−1). For every primitive embedding P→Λ_K3, the rational orthogonal complement is isometric to V_P.

Let S be projective K3, t=dim_Q T, V=T(1), and W=C⁺(T,q)=H¹(A,Q). Suppose one exact j_w tensor, for rational nonisotropic w and a rational polarization, is induced by CH²(S×A²)_Q. For every 1≤k≤t there is an injective algebraic Hodge map F_k:Λ^kV→End(W) with algebraic left inverse on cohomology. Every rational Hodge class in Λ^kV is a codimension-k rational algebraic cycle class on S^k.

For smooth projective X,Y of dimensions N,D and any C∈CH^{N+p}(X×Y)_Q with p≥0, there is a fixed closed B⊂Y of codimension at least p supporting the entire cohomological image of C. In particular C_*H^j(X,Q)⊂N^pH^{j+2p}(Y,Q) for every j.

Let V=T(1) for a projective K3 with Hg(V)=SO(V,q), t=dim V≥3. Let H be a nontrivial rational simple representation occurring in a direct sum of tensor powers of V, with its induced weight-zero Hodge structure of Hodge level at most 2b. Then there are c,s≥1 and integers 1≤k_i≤t with c≤b and s=Σk_i, and a surjective rational Hodge map ⊗_{i=1}^c Λ^{k_i}V→H.

For the stated smooth abelian double-cover data there is a smooth double cover Y→K=Km(B'), K resolved, such that: (i) V=H²(Y,Z)^{δ=−1} modulo torsion is even of signature (2,14) with 2-elementary discriminant group, and fixed-(B,M,χ) monodromy is trivial on that group; (ii) eight mutually orthogonal algebraic anti-invariant classes a_i of square −4 have perpendicular U⊂V_Q of signature (2,6), rationally isometric to V_P with the Y intersection form; (iii) resolved pullback gives a flat Hodge isomorphism β:U≅U_X with (βx,βy)_X=2(x,y)_Y, and e=(Δ_X+Γ_j−Γ_δ−Γ_{jδ})/4∈CH²(X×X)_Q has image U_X in degree two and vanishes in every other degree. Set E=T_B(−log D). U_X admits a flat complex identification with a character eigenspace having U_X^{p,q}≅H^q(B,Ω_B^p(log D)⊗M^−1χ), p+q=2; in particular U_X^{2,0}=H⁰(B,Mχ) is one-dimensional. The period map of U, equivalently U_X, has rank six on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the six-dimensional parameter space. For very general parameters U is simple, has no nonzero rational (1,1) class, and has Hodge group SO(U).

On a nonempty Zariski-open set of (B,D) parameters, D has no nontrivial translation stabilizer, C=D/{±1} is smooth of genus three, and D→C is a connected étale double cover defined by nontrivial ε∈Pic⁰(C)[2]. Let b be a construction point of final:curves. If a projective K3 S admits a rational Hodge isometry r_T:T_S≅U_b=T_{S⁰_b} for their cup forms, then for every full even-Clifford A for T_S, every rational nonisotropic right factor w and every rational polarization E, there is Γ_S∈CH²(S×A×A)_Q with Γ_S*x=ι_{w,E}(x) for all x∈T_S, as equality in the full H²(A²,Q).

For every K3 S with an ample primitive P-polarization, put U_P=P_Q-perpendicular⊂H²(S,Q). There exist a full W_U=C⁺(U_P,q)=H¹(A_U,Q), rational polarization E₀, rational nonisotropic w₀∈U_P, and Γ_U∈CH²(S×A_U²)_Q whose entire degree-two action on every x∈U_P is exactly ι_{w₀,E₀}(x), including the rational (1,1) classes in U_P at a Picard jump.

Let f:Z→B be a smooth proper holomorphic family of pure dimension n over a connected coordinate ball, with a closed relative embedding into P^N×B. Fix 0≤r≤n, a rational local system V, a morphism L:R^{2r}f_*Q→V, and a flat τ∈H⁰(B,V). The points b admitting a rational codimension-r cycle Z_b with L_b(cl(Z_b))=τ_b form a countable union of closed analytic subsets, each the image of a proper analytic parameter space carrying a fixed rational combination of universal flat subschemes; every point supplies an actual successful cycle. If that successful set contains a nonempty open, or escapes every countable union of proper closed analytic subsets, it equals B.

For every rational quadratic (V,q) of signature (2,n), O(V)(Q) is dense in O(V_R), and the rational orthogonal orbit of every point of its type-IV period domain meets every nonempty open subset of that domain.

Let i:W_T→W_U be an inclusion of polarizable rational weight-one Hodge structures, p:W_U→W_T a Hodge retraction, E_U,E_T rational polarizations, H a rational weight-zero Hodge structure, and j:H→End(W_U) a Hodge map. Put b=(E_T^flat)^−1 i∨(−1) E_U^flat. For the tensor form ι_{j,E_U}:H(−1)→W_U⊗W_U, (p⊗b)ι_{j,E_U}=ι_{pji,E_T}. When the weight-one spaces are abelian H¹, both slot maps are induced by rational algebraic correspondences.

For every ample P-polarized K3 S and every prescribed rational nonisotropic w∈T_S, rational polarization E and transported full even-Clifford realization C⁺(T_S,q), the exact standard ι_{w,E} admits a rational codimension-two algebraic realization.

If a projective K3 S has a rational isometric embedding T_S→V_P, there is an ample P-polarized K3 R and a full rational Hodge isometry Φ:H²(S,Q)≅H²(R,Q) with Φ(T_S)=T_R. Both Φ and Φ^−1 are induced by algebraic correspondences.
Under main:theorem's rational isometric-embedding hypothesis, the exact tensor ι_{w,E} on T_S is algebraic for every stipulated w, E and transported isogenous full even-Clifford model.

For every smooth projective complex K3 S with (T_S,q) rationally isometrically embedded in V_P, every n,r≥1 has HC and GHC in every degree of (S^[n])^r. More generally, for α∈Br(S), if M is a smooth projective moduli space of Gieseker-stable α-twisted sheaves on S, or of σ-stable objects in D^b(S,α) for a generic Bridgeland stability σ, then HC and GHC hold in every degree of M^r for every r≥1. If M is hyperkähler, the same holds for every smooth projective hyperkähler variety birational to M and all its self-powers.

For every smooth projective complex X and every r, the rational cycle class CH^r(X)_Q→H^{2r}(X,Q)∩H^{r,r}(X) is surjective. The manuscript claims this only for its stated K3 powers and transferred varieties, not for all X.

For every smooth projective complex X, degree j and coniveau p, N^pH^j(X,Q) equals the largest rational sub-Hodge structure whose types (a,b) have a,b≥p. The manuscript's conclusions are restricted to its stated families.

For a general projective K3 outside any asserted locus, algebraicity of one exact tensor of j_w(v)(a)=vaw on the full C⁺(T_S,q), with one rational nonisotropic w and one rational polarization, is the premise of ext:criterion. An arbitrary nonzero algebraic Hodge embedding, or an absolutely Hodge/motivated tensor without a cycle, is not that premise.

The locus hypothesis is the existence of a rational isometric embedding (T_S,q_cup)→V_P. It concerns the actual cup form, not merely rank, signature, an abstract Hodge embedding, or a differently rescaled form.

The classical KS construction produces the relevant abelian varieties and distinguished Hodge correspondence; that correspondence is absolutely Hodge and motivated. Algebraicity of the specified map is an additional assertion, not supplied by these imports.

For a projective K3's simple transcendental T, E=End_Hdg(T) is a number field, totally real or CM. The q-adjoint is respectively identity or conjugation. In the totally real case a nondegenerate symmetric E-form φ has trace q and Hg(T(1))=Res_{E/Q}SO(T,φ); in the CM case φ is Hermitian over E/E⁺ and Hg(T(1))=Res_{E⁺/Q}U(T,φ), the full unitary group. Hodge tensors are the invariants of these rational groups.

Every full rational Hodge isometry H²(S,Q)≅H²(S',Q) between smooth projective complex K3 surfaces is induced by a rational codimension-two algebraic correspondence. The source does not require integrality, preservation of an ample chamber, or equality of integral Néron–Severi lattices. Transcendental isometries are first extended by Witt to full H² isometries.

Over a splitting algebraic closure, SO invariants in arbitrary tensor powers of its nondegenerate standard module are spanned by metric contractions and a volume tensor. GL invariants on standard and dual slots are spanned by complete pair contractions, with equal numbers of standard and dual slots. The claimed spanning assertions have no stable-range restriction.

For primitive ample ADE polarizations, primitive big-and-nef smooth polarizations and the full integral period stack over C, the source imports existence/factorization of contraction q and the representable surjective étale quasi-polarized period map. The full Hodge-line linearization and exact stabilizer kernel in pencil:periodstack are additional arguments in this manuscript, not silently attributed to the existence theorem.

For the smooth projective threefold resolution in pencil:uniruledcriterion, non-pseudoeffectivity of its canonical class implies uniruledness; the source then uses birational invariance to pass to all smooth projective models.

For the smooth projective relative product over I and a smooth projective compactification, the image of compactification H⁴ in a fiber is the monodromy-invariant part. Because restriction is a map of polarizable pure Hodge structures, a flat rational (2,2) fiber tensor has a rational (2,2) lift. The lift is not asserted algebraic before the uniruled-threefold argument.

The invariant part of a geometric polarized variation is a constant Hodge subvariation. Restriction from a smooth projective compactification to a smooth open has image the lowest weight; in the application eH³(E_s^X) has pure polarizable W₃ part T_s, onto which the projected compactification H³ maps.

For the disjoint smooth divisor boundary D⊂Y^X, localization H²(D)(−1)→H⁴(Y^X)→H⁴(Y^X\D) is exact in canonical mixed Hodge structures. Proper Gysin and restriction are mixed-Hodge morphisms with codimension-one shift [−2](−1), and lowest-weight cohomology is polarizable. Strictness later controls the weight-four boundary error.

On a smooth ambient fiber, a coherent sheaf supported in codimension at least r has degree-r Chern character equal to its codimension-r fundamental cycle with generic lengths. GRR, dévissage and algebraic/topological Chern-class compatibility supply this identity; supports of codimension at least r+1 contribute no cohomology below degree 2r+2. The manuscript separately argues that the universal sheaf has the required resolution and restriction behavior over singular Hilbert parameters.
The rational Chow motive h(S^[n]) decomposes into Tate twists of summands of motives of powers of S; symmetric-product summands use rational averaging projectors.

Milne's pairing rationality asks that after good reduction a rational Hodge class have rational complementary divisor-product pairings, with one rational value in all realizations even for new nonlifting divisors. The manuscript states its precise claimed solution in thm:main; its cited antecedent pairing formulation is Milne2009 Conjecture 4.1 and MilneAIM2007 Section 10.

As described here, weak rationality asks that a specialized CM Hodge class whose components lie in the local spans of divisor products in every realization arise from one rational Lefschetz class. Only this manuscript's description is inventoried; the external full conjecture has not been read.

The source describes Milne's question whether a specialized CM Hodge class and a divisor lift together, up to isogeny, to a CM variety, and a conditional rationality criterion through weak lifting of Lefschetz classes on CM Weil triples. These are historical antecedents, not assumptions substituted for this manuscript's local prescribed-filtration construction; the source does not reproduce the full external statements.

Transport alternative (2) requires a degree-(0,1) weakly admissible filtration on D_A over a finite extension of K₀, finite local-field descent together with the specialized G-structure tensors, and membership after geometric tensor-preserving identification in the G-orbit of the original Hodge filtration. Weak admissibility alone without these other hypotheses is not the stated input.

The filtration theorem requires an invertible rational endomorphism u of the reduced abelian variety, Rosati self-adjoint and conjugate-linear over the given CM field: ue=bar e u for all e. The main argument does not assume such a u always exists: prop:weil treats its nonexistence by a zero-pairing branch.

The source invokes OpenAI's 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties', Theorem 1.1, to represent every rational Hodge class on the complex CM auxiliary B by a rational algebraic cycle. This is an additional input solely to cor:algebraic-specialization, not to the rationality theorem or CM transport. That October 6 manuscript was not among the assigned sources and was not read.

Every Hodge class on an abelian variety is absolute Hodge; its p-adic realization has the comparison compatibility invoked in lem:comparison, including the perfect-residue-field version for local auxiliary lifts. This supplies compatible realizations, not rational intersections with new divisors by itself.

For an abelian X/F, Lef^r(X) realizes injectively and its scalar extension is the divisor-generated subspace in every relevant cohomology, including crystalline. Intersection gives a perfect rational pairing with Lef^{dim X−r}; homomorphism pushforward preserves local divisor-generated subspaces; hard Lefschetz and its inverse restrict to them. Extension from crystalline coefficients to C_w preserves these statements.

For the good-reduction abelian schemes over a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with perfect residue field, full faithfulness of rational filtered Dieudonné modules is invoked to turn a Frobenius-compatible filtration-preserving crystalline map into a rational map of p-divisible groups (equivalently of Tate modules via crystalline comparison). The input in lem:lift-hom is already a rational algebraic special-fiber homomorphism.

After one integer clears both the Tate-lattice and prescribed f₀ denominators, Tate's extension theorem extends the resulting integral generic-fiber p-divisible-group map over R. Faithfulness of the special-fiber Dieudonné functor and torsion-freeness identify its reduction with Nf₀.

Specified-map Serre–Tate deformation theory supplies compatible lifts over R/m^n of an algebraic special-fiber homomorphism together with the matching p-divisible-group lift. Formal existence algebraizes the resulting map when its source is proper over the complete noetherian R and target separated of finite type. The source's shear argument connects the fixed-object formulation to specified maps.

\label{p3ab:split-sixfolds}
Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field and let \(A\) be a complex
abelian sixfold with an \(E\)-action.  Suppose a compatible
polarization has hyperbolic rational Hermitian form of signature
\((3,3)\).  Then the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every
codimension on \(A^m\), for every \(m\geq1\).

\label{p3ab:quadratic-five}
Let \(A\) be a complex abelian variety of dimension at most five
admitting an action of an imaginary quadratic field.  The rational
Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on \(A^m\), for every
\(m\geq1\).

\label{p3:cm-operations}
CM supply is preserved by external products, permutations of factors,
cup products, and rational algebraic correspondences.  It is also
preserved by $k$-linear combinations of such correspondences and by
scalar conjugation.  Every rational Hodge class in a CM-supplied
subspace is algebraic.

\label{p3:admissible-operations}
Every admissible map is induced on the indicated summands by a
$k$-linear combination of rational algebraic correspondences.
Every pair tensor is algebraic over $k$, and contraction by its
inverse pairing is an algebraic cohomological operation.
If $W$ is admissible, so is $\overline W$, and there is a pair
tensor between $W$ and $\overline W$.

\label{p3:tensor-stabilizer}
Inside the symplectic group of $H$, the group
$\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$ is the pointwise stabilizer of all rational
tensors of type $(a,a)$ in $H^{\otimes 2a}$, for all $a\ge0$.

\label{p3:toric-cm-factor}
Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety and let $H\subset H^1(A,\Q)$ be a
rational Hodge summand.  If $\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$ is a torus, then
$H$ is isomorphic as a rational Hodge structure to $H^1(B,\Q)$ for a
CM isogeny factor $B$ of $A$.

\label{p3:tensor-criterion}
Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety, $H=H^1(A,\Q)$,
$J=\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$, and $R=J^{\mathrm{der}}$.
Suppose the following data exist.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\alph*)}]
\item A rational Hodge summand $H_0\subset H$ has toric Hodge group.
Choose a decomposition of $H_{0,k}$ into CM embedding lines,
with repeated occurrences distinguished, and call this finite list
$\mathcal E_0$.
\item The complement of $H_{0,k}$ is a direct sum of blocks of
nonzero admissible spaces.  In a symplectic or an orthogonal block,
each space is equipped with an admissible isomorphism to a
representative $V_i$ chosen as an actual summand of that block,
with, respectively, an alternating or a
symmetric pair tensor on itself.  A linear block has
$\dim V_i\ge2$, with $V_i$ again an actual summand, and each space is equipped with an admissible
isomorphism to either $V_i$ or $\overline V_i$, paired with
each other as in Lemma~\ref{p3:admissible-operations}.
The pair identifies $\overline V_i$ with $V_i^*(-1)$ as a
Hodge-graded space and with the dual as a group representation.
\item Under these identifications the image of $R_k$ contains
\[
 P=\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{Sp}}}\operatorname{Sp}(V_i)
   \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}}\operatorname{SO}(V_i)
   \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}}\operatorname{SL}(V_i).
\]
Each factor acts by its standard representation on its own copies,
by the dual representation on the opposite copies of a linear
block, and trivially on every other block and on $H_{0,k}$.
The symplectic and orthogonal forms are the inverse pairings.
\item Let $W_1,\ldots,W_s$ be any list, with arbitrary repetitions,
from
\[
 \{V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}\}
 \ \cup\
 \{V_i,\overline V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}\}.
\]
Whenever there are $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r\in\mathcal E_0$, again
with arbitrary repetitions, such that
\begin{equation}
 \label{p3:eq:determinant-balance}
 \sum_{j=1}^s\epsilon_\gamma(W_j)
 +\sum_{a=1}^r\epsilon_\gamma(\ell_a)=0
 \quad\text{for every }\gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/\Q),
\end{equation}
the line $\bigotimes_{j=1}^sD(W_j)$ is CM-supplied on its
separate tensor slots.  Empty lists are allowed.
\end{enumerate}

Then for every $p\ge0$ every rational balanced tensor in $H^{\otimes 2p}$ is the
class of a rational algebraic cycle on its separate $A$-slots.
The rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension of $A^m$
for every $m\ge1$.

Call the data \emph{saturated} if every singleton $D(V_i)$ for
an orthogonal or linear block is CM-supplied, without any balance
condition.  For saturated data and any CM abelian variety $M$,
the induced data on $A\times M$ are saturated.  In particular the
same tensor and Hodge-conjecture conclusions hold for every power of
$A\times M$.

\label{p3:correspondence-transfer}
Let $\mathscr S$ be a collection of smooth projective varieties such
that the rational Hodge conjecture holds on every finite product of
members of $\mathscr S$.  Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_v$ be smooth projective
varieties.  Suppose that, for each $i$ and each degree $q$,
$H^q(Y_i,\Q)$ is spanned by images of maps
\[
 \Gamma_*:H^{q-2j}(S,\Q)\longrightarrow H^q(Y_i,\Q),
 \qquad
 \Gamma\in\CH^{\dim S+j}(S\times Y_i)_\Q,\quad S\in\mathscr S.
\]
Then the rational Hodge conjecture holds on every
finite product of the $Y_i$, with arbitrary repetitions and with
any additional members of $\mathscr S$.

The same conclusion holds if the spanning is given over $k$ by
restrictions of maps induced by $k$-linear combinations of
rational algebraic correspondences, provided their images span
the full target degree after scalar extension.

\label{p3sw:weil-plane}
Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field.  Let \(A\) be a complex
abelian sixfold with a unital \(E\)-action and a compatible polarization
whose actual homological Hermitian form \(h_E\) is hyperbolic of signature
\((3,3)\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal W_E(A)\ \subset\
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(\CH^3(A)_\Q
                    \longrightarrow H^6(A,\Q)\bigr).
\]
The assertion holds at every compatible period, including nonsimple
varieties and periods with additional endomorphisms.

\label{p3ab:hyperbolic}
Let \(E\) be imaginary quadratic.  A nondegenerate \(E\)-Hermitian
form of rank \(2b\) and signature \((b,b)\), \(b\geq1\), is
hyperbolic if and only if
\[
 [\det h]=[(-1)^b].
\]
Every hyperbolic form of this rank is isometric to the sum of \(b\)
planes with matrix
\(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).

\label{p3ab:determinant-supply}
Let \(A\) be a complex abelian variety with an action of an imaginary
quadratic field \(E\), and let a compatible rational Riemann form
have associated Hermitian form of signature \((p,q)\).
Put \(n=\dim A=p+q\).  Both lines
\[
 D\bigl(H^1(A,k)_\sigma\bigr),\qquad
 D\bigl(H^1(A,k)_{\bar\sigma}\bigr)
\]
are CM-supplied in either of the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(n=6\), \((p,q)=(3,3)\), and the form is hyperbolic;
\item \(n<6\) and \(p,q\leq3\).
\end{enumerate}
The second assertion permits every compatible rational Riemann form.
Both assertions hold at every period.

\label{p3ab:albert-columns}
In Types I--III let \(F=Z(D)\) be totally real of degree \(f\).
In Type IV let the CM center \(K=Z(D)\) have degree \(2f\), and
write \([D:K]=b^2\).  The columns in
\eqref{p3ab:eq:columns} have the following data:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
 \text{Albert type}&\text{necessary divisibility}&\dim_k W&
       \text{pair tensor}\\ \hline
 \mathrm I& f\mid g&2g/f&\text{alternating on }W\\
 \mathrm{II}&2f\mid g&g/f&\text{alternating on }W\\
 \mathrm{III}&2f\mid g&g/f&\text{symmetric on }W\\
 \mathrm{IV}&fb^2\mid g&g/(fb)&\text{between opposite columns}.
\end{array}
\]
The listed tensors are pair tensors in the sense of
Section~\ref{p3:sec:tensors}, and all copy identifications are
admissible.  In Type IV the opposite column is the dual
\(R_B\)-module.

\label{p3ab:minuscule}
In the irreducible tensor decomposition of a column \(W_\tau\) for
the simple ideals of \(\operatorname{Lie}(R_B)_k\), every nontrivial
simple factor representation is minuscule.

\label{p3ab:small-projections}
An alternating self-paired column of dimension \(2,4\), or \(6\)
has the full symplectic derived image.  A symmetric self-paired
column cannot have dimension two; in dimensions four and six its
derived image is, respectively, the full \(\operatorname{SO}_4\)
and \(\operatorname{SO}_6\).

If \(D=K\) is an imaginary quadratic field, \(B\) is non-CM, and
\(\dim_K H_B\leq6\), then the derived image on either embedding
column is the full special linear group, with dual action on the
opposite column.

\label{p3ab:small-columns}
Let \(A\) have an imaginary-quadratic \(E\)-action and
\(\dim A\leq6\).  Write \(A\sim\prod_B B^{r_B}\) with pairwise
nonisogenous simple factors, and discard the CM factors.  Put
\(g=\dim B\).  After identifying matrix copies, the remaining
columns have the following possibilities.
\begin{enumerate}
\item In Types I and II they have full symplectic derived images
and dimensions \(2,4,6\).
\item In Type III, \(g=4\) or \(6\), the center is \(\Q\), and
\(r_B=1\).  The unique column has full
\(\operatorname{SO}_g\) image.  Each eigenspace of the given
\(E\)-action is one copy of this column and has equal Hodge
multiplicities \(g/2,g/2\).
\item In Type IV, \(D=K\) is a CM field.  If \(E\) admits no
\(\Q\)-embedding into \(K\), then \(K\) is imaginary quadratic,
\(g=3\), and \(r_B=2\); the \(K\)-columns have the full
\(\operatorname{SL}_3\) and dual images.

If \(E\) admits a \(\Q\)-embedding into \(K\), put
\([K:\Q]=2f\) and \(a=g/f\).  The possibilities are
\[
 f=1,\quad 3\leq a=g\leq6;

\]
Every column has the full \(\operatorname{SL}_a\) image,
paired with the dual at the opposite embedding.  In the cases
with \(a=2\), some embedding pairs are mixed and some are pure.
\end{enumerate}
All these are projections of the actual derived Hodge group of \(A\).

For every complex abelian variety A of dimension at most six with a unital imaginary-quadratic action, the actual derived Hodge-group images on non-CM Albert columns are the full independent classical groups in the manuscript's small-column list, after admissible matrix-copy identifications and pairing opposite CM embeddings. This verifies condition (c), not determinant supply, central-character independence, or the Hodge conjecture.

For the actual polarized weight-one Hodge structure of a simple abelian factor, the rational Hodge group is connected reductive, its commutant is the full opposite endomorphism division algebra, and Albert columns have the divisibilities, multiplicities and polarization-pairing signs used in the small-column reduction.

Hodge-circle minimality and the two weights +1,-1 imply that every nontrivial simple-ideal constituent of every actual Albert column is minuscule, including constituents at pure embeddings after scalar transport.

The dimension-six budget and a unital imaginary-quadratic action force exactly the manuscript's necessary list of non-CM column projections; this is a covering list, not an assertion that every numerical tuple is realized by an abelian variety.
